visual_review.method: exact-artifact MapLibre tolerance=0; fit plus two boundary-focused zooms centered on the candidate point with maximum approximate nearest-source displacement

existing_live_exception.reason: The live Achaemenid pilot was explicitly visually accepted before the 10 km default was adopted. D-049 forbids replacing it merely for uniformity.

features.name: Western Han China
features.semantic_scope_note: The reviewed claim concerns private and government slavery across the Western Han polity while explicitly limiting prevalence claims; the polity geometry is used as historical context, not as a claim of uniform practice intensity.

features.name: Mauryan Empire
features.semantic_scope_note: The reviewed claim is a polity-period synthesis for Mauryan-period India and explicitly avoids treating slavery as the economic basis of the empire; the geometry is contextual rather than a uniform-prevalence footprint.

features.name: New Kingdom Egypt
features.semantic_scope_note: The reviewed claim is a broad New Kingdom synthesis covering institutional and military enslavement/servitude; the selected polity geometry is a defensible historical context layer.

features.name: Hittite central Anatolia
features.semantic_scope_note: The reviewed claims synthesize Hittite legal and institutional non-free categories; the central-Anatolia polity geometry is a bounded contextual extent and does not collapse all dependency categories into slavery.

features.name: Roman Empire — early Principate
features.semantic_scope_note: The reviewed claim is explicitly empire-wide specialist synthesis describing Rome as a slave society; the polity extent is appropriate historical context, without implying identical local prevalence.

features.name: Baekje
features.semantic_scope_note: The reviewed evidence is a bounded 369 captive-enslavement event and explicitly does not establish prevalence across Baekje society. The whole-polity proxy is therefore semantically sensitive even apart from the failed cartographic QC.
